text:
marie: FYI I'm prototyping a hybrid preemptible eviction flow that tries a live stream swap first, then falls back to a resume-requeue. Want to keep p99 impact tiny.

aj: Nice. What's the basic handshake timeline? :eyes:

marie: Rough flow:
- node gets preempt signal -> mark as draining and stop new accepts
- for each active streaming request: mark as swap-candidate
- try in-memory swap handshake with candidate fallback worker (timeout 2s)
- if swap succeeds -> fallback takes over KV cursor and continues streaming to client
- if swap fails -> atomically enqueue resume job with resume-token and short TTL (15s)

santiago: How do we avoid duplicate tokens or repeated tool calls if a chunk was emitted right before the handoff?

marie: Commit semantics: only tokens that pass the local output-flush point are considered committed. We include a resume cursor referencing the last-committed-offset + KV keys. For tool calls we attach a dedupe-id to each invocation; requeued requests will re-run but check dedupe table first.

alex: Prototype handshake snippet (pseudo):

```
node.drain_start()
for stream in node.streams:
  stream.swap_pending = true
  ok = attempt_swap(stream, fallback, timeout_ms=2000)
  if ok:
    fallback.bind_kv(stream.kv_cursor)
    fallback.stream_to_client(stream.client_conn)
  else:
    enqueue_resume(stream, ttl_s=15)
```

marie: We'll also add a short preStop hook so kube stops sending new sessions immediately:

```
preStop:
  exec:
    command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "curl -sS -XPOST http://127.0.0.1:5200/drain && sleep 0.8"]
```

aj: If the fallback is in same AZ and also being drained we get correlated failures. Suggest prefer cross-AZ fallback when RTT < 30ms. Use placement hints.

marie: Agreed. Policy: prefer different AZ if estimated RTT < 30ms, otherwise local fallback. We'll surface routing hints from placement service.

oncall-bot: Alert: preempt event predicted for pool gpu-west-2b-11, ETA ~22s (eviction-watcher).

veda: Metrics to track for the experiment:
- hybrid_swap_attempts_total
- hybrid_swap_success_ratio
- resume_enqueue_rate
- resumed_stream_tail_latency_p50_p99
- token_duplication_count (should be 0)

santiago: Give me a PromQL for resumed p99 so SLOs can be gated:

```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(resumed_stream_tail_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```

alex: Important: keep handshake ephemeral and in-memory only. Do not persist handshake tokens to etcd. If handshake fails, requeue — no control-plane churn.

marie: Rollout plan:
1) canary: 2% of dev traffic on dev cluster for 6h (collect traces & metrics)
2) staging: 15% for 24h, validate edge cases
3) prod: 8% on low-priority routes (embeddings, batch transforms) for 48h
4) expand or rollback based on metrics

aj: Cost note: expect brief upswing in short-lived fallback tasks and resume re-executions -> track preemptible billing delta.

marie: We'll add a cost delta dashboard comparing spot CPU/GPU seconds and reserved usage during the window.

santiago: Edge-case: very long streams (>90s) are risky for mid-token swaps. Proposal: disable swap for streams >90s, always enqueue resume with longer TTL (30s) and stricter dedupe.

marie: OK cutover enabled only for streams <=90s and emission rate >=0.5 tok/s. Otherwise go straight to resume.

oncall-bot: Deploy queued: hybrid-evict-swap-prototype -> cluster/dev (submitted by marie).

alex: SDK impact: clients must tolerate a short reconnect or accept a resume header. Plan to add header X-Redwood-Resume: v1; value = resume-id so SDK can transparently continue.

veda: Add an alert: if hybrid_swap_success_ratio < 80% for 5m then auto-roll back the canary.

marie: I'll draft a short RFC and open SRE ticket SRE-EX-715 with runbook, PromQLs, and dashboards. Who can pair on the first canary run tomorrow?

aj: I can.

santiago: I can verify the dedupe/tool-call behavior.

alex: I'll land the SDK header change and a tiny client toleration test.

marie: Thanks. I'll post the RFC link here when ready. :thumbsup:
